one_month_reasoning: Little company-specific is scheduled before 2026-10-31. Hudbay reported Q3 2025 on 12 Nov 2025 and Q2 2026 on 29-30 Jul 2026, so Q3 2026 results most likely land in early-to-mid November, after the window. The Copper World sanction decision is guided for 'late 2026'. It could come in October, but more likely it lands in Q4 alongside or after the DFS release. A positive sanction is mostly expected already; the risk is capex or IRR headlines in either direction. The macro events in the window are the late-October FOMC meeting and China's October activity data, and both reach HBM mainly through copper. Kalshi's weekly copper markets in late September (about 66% that copper would be above $6.60/lb on 25 Sep) put copper near record highs. This beta-heavy name tends to amplify copper moves about 1.5-2x. With no dated catalyst, I used a symmetric lognormal around $26.18 at monthly vol of 0.63/3.5 = 18%, with a small negative median from the volatility drag. I added no momentum or reversal tilt because the stock is mid-range: it is down from the $32.15 June high and up from the $19.70 July low.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM EV/EBITDA ($1.30B x 7.5x plus $0.08B net cash, divided by ~442M shares = $22.2), 2027 P/E ($1.55 x 15x = $23.3) and FCF yield (~$450M normalized FCF at a 4% yield = $25.5), weighted 40/35/25 = about $23.5. Mid-cycle multiples are applied to near-record copper, so fair value sits slightly below the spot price.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA $1.30B x 7.5x = $9.75B EV; + $0.08B net cash; / ~442M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: LTM $1.27B lifted for higher H2-2026 output (BC mill improvements) and improved cash-cost guidance, then held back because Cochilco's 2027 copper forecast ($5.10/lb) is well below spot (~$6.3-6.6/lb). BofA's 2027 forecast of $6.12/lb is the upside case.

Mid-tier copper producers have historically traded around 5-8x mid-cycle EBITDA and de-rated sharply after copper peaks (2011 and 2015 routs, source 9). HBM is at roughly 9x LTM today. I used 7.5x: a premium to mid-cycle for net cash and the Copper World pipeline, but no peak-cycle multiple.

Q2 weighted basic of 400.4M plus 46.8M shares issued for the Arizona Sonoran (Cactus) acquisition gives about 442-447M. This is consistent with the ~$12.2B market cap at about $26 quoted by stocktitan.

H1-2026 run-rate of about $1.38/yr on the pre-acquisition share count, plus higher production. Stifel models $0.27/qtr for Q1-Q2 2027, about $1.10 on an older copper deck. Adjusted for higher copper and gold and diluted to ~442M shares, I land at about $1.55.
Trailing P/E is about 13.7x (source 4) at near-record metal prices. I used 15x on forward earnings to credit the growth pipeline, capped because miners de-rate when commodity prices roll over.
H1 annualized is about $400M. I added for H2 production weighting, net of rising New Ingerbelle and Arizona growth capex (BC growth capex raised to $115M).
A low required yield reflects net cash and the Mitsubishi-funded Copper World growth. It is not lower because copper is near a cyclical high.

bear.story: Copper mean-reverts toward Cochilco's $5.10 or lower (sub-$4.75/lb) as supply disruptions ease and US inventory overhang unwinds, and gold softens. Miners de-rate as in 2011, 2015 and 2022, when copper equities fell 35-55%. Copper World sanction brings capex inflation and EBITDA falls toward $0.8B.

base.story: Copper eases to $5.5-6.0/lb with gold strong. Production rises in BC, Copper World is sanctioned with Mitsubishi funding and the stock holds 7-8x EBITDA. History shows a roughly flat median one year after a >50% annual gain.

bull.story: Copper holds or exceeds $6.5/lb, in line with BofA's record 2027 call, on AI, grid and EV demand plus mine disruptions. Copper World's DFS and sanction re-rate the NAV and the stock retests and breaks the $32 high, as in the +65-90% follow-through years in its history.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $15.5 the stock would be back at pre-breakout levels from late 2025 (Nov 2025 low $14.34). That would imply the market is pricing copper well under $5/lb on a sustained basis, a damaging Copper World outcome (capex blowout or deferral) or a Peru/Constancia operating or political shock, rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise around a ~$24 fair value.

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: spot is ~$6.3-6.6/lb vs. Cochilco's 2027 forecast of $5.10 and BofA's $6.12. HBM equity runs at about 1.5-2x copper beta.
Gold by-product credits (38% of revenue) are what drive negative cash costs, so a gold correction hurts margins directly.
Copper World capex and sanction terms, and the dilution or financing needed beyond Mitsubishi's $600M.
Share count after the Arizona Sonoran deal (~442-447M) affects all per-share values.
Peru politics and social licence. Fujimori won the runoff by only ~0.3pp, and Peru has a history of congressional removals of presidents.
Mean reversion after a +77% year: historical HBM outcomes after >50% 12-month gains range from 0.52x to 1.9x.
reasoning: Base rates came first. I computed 137 overlapping 12-month log returns from HBM monthly closes since 2014 (Twelve Data). They show a median of about 1.09x, an interquartile range of 0.71x-1.64x and a standard deviation of 0.58 in log terms. Monthly-return annualized vol was 62% over the full history and 54% over the last 24 months. In 28 month-ends where the trailing 12-month gain exceeded 50% (overlapping, so small effective sample), the next 12 months had a median of about 1.05x and a range of 0.52x-1.9x, roughly a coin flip with fat tails both ways. The fat tails come from the 2011/2015-style copper equity routs and the 2020-21 and 2024-26 copper bull legs. The fundamentals cap the upside median: the stock is at roughly 9x record LTM EBITDA ($1.27B) with copper near all-time highs (Kalshi weeklies around $6.5-6.6/lb in late September). Forecasters expect lower 2027 prices (Cochilco $5.10; BofA is the bull at $6.12), and net cash plus the Mitsubishi-funded Copper World are already partly priced in. My blended fair value is about $23.5 (EV/EBITDA $22.2, P/E $23.3, FCF yield $25.5). I set the 12-month median at $25, between fair value and spot, which reflects momentum in a structurally tight copper market. I used a lognormal with sigma 0.56, a little below the realized 63% because the last 24 months ran at 54% and higher volatility usually goes with drawdowns. That gives P(>=26) of about 0.47, and the scenario mixture of 15/25/37 at 25/50/25 is consistent with it. Limits: Twelve Data stats and price targets and Alpha Vantage estimates were paywalled or rate-limited, and Kalshi pages returned 429, so I quote copper market odds from search snippets of the Kalshi market pages. I found no Polymarket or Manifold market on Hudbay-specific events. I did not consult option prices or implied volatility. The price series from Twelve Data shows an Oct-1 close of 27.20, which differs from the brief's $26.18. I used the brief's figure.
